<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**A [[mass shooting]] in [[Jaral del Progreso]], [[Guanajuato]], leaves at least 11 people dead and one injured. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mexico-crime-cartels/massacre-in-mexican-bar-leaves-11-people-dead-idUSKBN26I0Z6 (Reuters)]
*[[Nagorno-Karabakh conflict]]
**[[Second Nagorno-Karabakh War]]
***The [[Armed Forces of Armenia|Armenian]] and [[Azerbaijani Armed Forces|Azerbaijani]] armed forces clash along the border of the unrecognized [[Republic of Artsakh]], formerly known as the Nagorno-Karabakh Republic. Several cities in Artsakh, including its capital city of [[Stepanakert]], are under attack. At least 23 people are killed during the battle, of whom 16 are Nagorno-Karabakh servicemen, five Azerbaijani civilians and two Armenian civilians. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-54314341 (BBC News)]
***[[Armenia]] and the self-proclaimed Republic of Artsakh declare [[martial law]] and a full mobilization of its [[Artsakh Defence Army]] amid an Azerbaijani invasion. [[Azerbaijani Armed Forces]] say they have captured six Armenian villages. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/sep/27/armenia-martial-law-clashes-azerbaijan (''The Guardian'')]
***In a live televised address to the nation, [[Prime Minister of Armenia|Armenian Prime Minister]] [[Nikol Pashinyan]] declares a general mobilization and orders citizens to "get ready to defend our sacred homeland", following the clashes with Azerbaijan in [[Nagorno-Karabakh]]. [https://www.thenational.ae/world/europe/armenia-rallies-to-defend-homeland-over-fighting-with-azerbaijan-1.1084026 (''The National'')]
***[[Azerbaijanis|Azerbaijani]] [[President of Azerbaijan|President]] [[Ilham Aliyev]] declares martial law, and imposes curfews from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m. in major cities, including the capital [[Baku]], in response to the clashes between Azeri and Armenian forces in Nagorno-Karabakh. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-armenia-azerbaijan-curfew-idUKKBN26I0OS (Reuters)] [https://www.aninews.in/news/world/asia/azerbaijans-president-approves-martial-law-curfew-in-parts-of-country20200927225634/ (ANI)]
***[[Azerbaijan]]'s [[Ministry of Defence (Azerbaijan)|Ministry of Defence]] says advancing Azerbaijani troops have "liberated" the strategic [[Murovdag]] mountain peak, which was the scene of a previous battle in 1993, that ended in Armenian victory. [https://en.trend.az/azerbaijan/politics/3306285.html (Trend)]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**The [[Special Envoy of the Secretary-General|United Nations Special Envoy]] for [[Yemen]] [[Martin Griffiths]] announces that the [[Houthis]] and the [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]]-backed [[Yemeni government]] have agreed to a [[prisoner swap]] of 1,081 detainees. The release will include 400 government prisoners and 681 Houthi fighters. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-yemen-security-un/yemen-warring-parties-agree-to-exchange-1081-prisoners-u-n-envoy-idUSKBN26I0EV?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*[[China–United States trade war]], [[Censorship of TikTok]]
**The [[United States District Court for the District of Columbia|U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia]] temporarily blocks [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]]'s [[executive order]] banning [[TikTok]] from smartphone [[app store]]s hours before it was to go into effect, after lawyers representing the app's company [[ByteDance]] argued its ban would constitute a form of [[censorship]]. [https://www.npr.org/2020/09/27/917452668/u-s-judge-halts-trumps-tiktok-ban-hours-before-it-was-set-to-start#:~:text=A%20federal%20judge%20on%20Sunday,speech%20and%20due%20process%20rights. (NPR)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[Premier of Victoria|Victorian premier]] [[Daniel Andrews]] announces a plan to lift a nighttime curfew between 9:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. ([[Time in Australia|AEST]]) local time in [[Melbourne]] and ease many restrictions across [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]], including returning pupils to school and relaxing restrictions on outdoor gatherings effective tomorrow. However, the state introduces a fine of almost $5,000 for those violating any gathering rules. [https://amp.theguardian.com/australia-news/2020/sep/27/melbourne-covid-curfew-ends-and-restrictions-ease-but-victoria-introduces-huge-new-fines (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
***The number of daily new cases in the [[Netherlands]] hits a record 2,995 cases in the past 24 hours, according to data from health ministry. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-netherlands-tally/dutch-corona-cases-reach-daily-record-of-2995-health-authorities-idUSL8N2GO0CN (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[2020 Belarusian protests]]
**[[Ministry of Internal Affairs (Belarus)|Police]] carry out mass arrests as thousands of people gather for new protests; more than 50 protesters are arrested. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-54316568 (BBC News)]
*[[2020 Swiss referendums]]
**[[Swiss people|Swiss]] voters reject the proposal, from the [[right-wing]] [[Swiss People's Party]], to end an accord with the [[European Union]] that allows free movement of people. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-54316316 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Tax returns of Donald Trump]]
**''[[The New York Times]]'' reports that it has obtained more than two decades of tax-return data for Donald Trump and his business enterprises, including [[The Trump Organization]]. The documents show that Trump paid no [[federal income tax]] in 11 of the last 15 years, and paid just [[United States dollar|$]]750 in income taxes in 2016, and $750 in 2017. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-54319948 (BBC News)]

;Sports
*[[2020 NBA playoffs]]
**The [[Miami Heat]] advance to the [[2020 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] with a 125–113 victory against the [[Boston Celtics]] in game 6. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/national/miami-heat-advance-to-nba-finals-against-los-angeles-lakers-beating-boston-celtics-125-113-in-game-6-of-eastern-finals/2020/09/27/51e7211a-012f-11eb-b92e-029676f9ebec_story.html (''Washington Post'')]
